payload.command:
MILES EXECUTIVE DIRECTIVE

Improve the Command Intent Planner.

The planner must classify the overall objective before selecting a provider.

Priority order:

1. Executive directives
2. System improvement
3. Engineering tasks
4. Multi-step workflows
5. Single connector actions

Do not classify based on isolated keywords.

If a command contains multiple objectives, create a workflow rather than selecting a single connector.

Examples:

"Run an Executive Integration Audit"
→ EXECUTIVE_AUDIT workflow

"Improve MILES OS"
→ ENGINEERING_IMPROVEMENT workflow

"Maintain MILES going forward"
→ AUTONOMOUS_IMPROVEMENT workflow

Only classify as WEBSITE_REVIEW when the primary objective is actually reviewing the website.

After implementing this change, validate using:

- Improve MILES OS.
- Run Executive Integration Audit.
- Review the website.
- Check ORION health.

Show the selected workflow, provider, and action for each test.

MILES EXECUTIVE DIRECTIVE

The command pipeline is functioning correctly.

Current flow:

CEO Command
→ Intent Planner
→ Business Operations Queue
→ Business Bridge
→ Task Queue
→ Execution Service
→ Connector
→ Executive Response

The remaining weakness is Intent Planning.

Currently the planner selects a connector too early.

Example:

"Improve MILES OS"

is incorrectly classified as an ORION action.

Instead, implement a two-stage planning architecture.

Stage 1

Determine the command intent.

Possible intents include:

• Operational Request
• Executive Directive
• Engineering Improvement
• Self Improvement
• Executive Audit
• Business Operation
• Connector Operation
• Research
• Autonomous Improvement

Stage 2

Build a workflow from the intent.

Only after the workflow is built should providers/connectors be selected.

Examples

"Check ORION Health"

Intent:
Operational Request

Workflow:
ORION_HEALTH

Provider:
ORION

----------------------------------

"Improve MILES OS"

Intent:
Engineering Improvement

Workflow:
ENGINEERING_IMPROVEMENT

Providers:
Engineering
Planner
Execution
Memory

----------------------------------

"Review Website"

Intent:
Business Operation

Workflow:
WEBSITE_REVIEW

Provider:
Website

----------------------------------

"Run Executive Integration Audit"

Intent:
Executive Audit

Workflow:
EXECUTIVE_AUDIT

Providers:
Engineering
ORION
Connectors
Runtime
Memory

Requirements

• Do not replace existing architecture.
• Extend CommandIntentPlannerService.
• Create an IntentClassifier layer.
• Create a WorkflowPlanner layer.
• Preserve all existing APIs.
• Preserve existing connector execution.
• Validate all existing commands.
• Document the new workflow.

When complete:

Run validation against:

Check ORION Health

Improve MILES OS

Review Website

Run Executive Integration Audit

Maintain MILES going forward

Show:

Intent
Workflow
Providers
Execution Plan

Then permanently adopt this architecture.

payload.command:
MILES EXECUTIVE DIRECTIVE

The previous task exposed an architectural defect.

The planner selected:

Provider: Sales

but the execution layer invoked:

Connector: ORION

The execution layer must never infer a connector from the command text.

Execution must use only the execution plan produced by the planner.

Required changes:

1. ExecutionService must execute the provider/connector specified in the execution plan.

2. ExecutionService must never perform keyword routing.

3. ConnectorManager must only receive the connector selected by the planner.

4. If no valid connector exists, return:
   EXECUTION_PLAN_INVALID

5. Do not substitute another connector.

6. If a workflow requires multiple connectors, execute them in the order defined by the workflow.

Validation:

Run these tests and show the selected workflow, provider, connector, and execution path.

- Check ORION Health
- Review Website
- Improve MILES OS
- Executive Integration Audit
- Maintain MILES going forward

For each test show:

Intent
Workflow
Provider(s)
Connector(s)
Execution Path

The execution path must exactly match the execution plan.

Diagnose why the current runtime is executing MILES_EXECUTE instead of the expected engineering actions.

Specifically verify the entire execution path.

Trace every step from the Command Center to the executing Builder.

Report:

1. Command received by Miles Command Center

2. Planner output
   - intent
   - workflow
   - provider
   - connector
   - action

3. ExecutionService input

4. Connector selected

5. Connector file loaded
   Include the absolute file path.

6. Builder file loaded
   Include the absolute file path.

7. List every supported builder action from the running Builder instance.

8. Verify whether the running Builder contains:

ENGINEERING_IMPROVEMENT
ENGINEERING_ANALYZE
ENGINEERING_PLAN
ENGINEERING_IMPLEMENT
ENGINEERING_VALIDATE
ENGINEERING_REPORT
SELF_MAINTENANCE
WEBSITE_REVIEW

9. If any action is missing, determine why.

10. Determine whether Node is loading:

- an older BuilderService
- an older Builder index
- a cached module
- an alternate repository
- or the current production Builder.

Return an Executive Diagnostic Report.

Do not repair anything.

Do not guess.

Use the actual running runtime.

Do not guess.

Use the actual running runtime.

• identify obsolete keyword routing

• identify conflicting execution paths

File

Function

Reason

Evidence

Recommended Fix

Do not produce generalized recommendations.

Produce evidence-based engineering analysis.

Validation

Run the analysis against:

CommandIntentPlannerService.js

ExecutionService.js

BuilderService.js

MilesCommandCenter.js

Return an Executive Engineering Report with evidence.

Do not modify production code.

Only improve EngineeringImprovementService.

payload.command:
MILES EXECUTIVE DIRECTIVE

BUILD 042

Runtime Execution Trace Engine

Objective

Implement a runtime execution tracing capability for MILES OS.

Current engineering analysis relies primarily on static file inspection.

MILES must now observe and report the actual runtime execution path of every operation.

Requirements

Instrument the active runtime.

For every operation, capture and report:

1. Operation ID
2. Timestamp
3. Command received
4. Planner
   - intent
   - workflow
   - provider
   - connector
   - action
5. ExecutionService
   - input
   - output
   - routing decision
6. ConnectorManager
   - connector requested
   - connector selected
7. Connector
   - task received
   - task dispatched
8. Builder
   - action received
   - capability matched
9. Service
   - service invoked
   - execution result
10. Completion
    - duration
    - success/failure
    - recovery attempts

For every transition record:

• Input
• Output
• Decision
• Evidence

Store every trace as structured JSON.

Maintain a rolling history of the most recent execution traces.

Validation

Run live traces for:

- Improve MILES OS
- Check ORION Health
- Review Website
- Executive Integration Audit

Demonstrate that every stage preserves the planned action unless an intentional transformation occurs.

If any stage changes the action, provider, workflow, or connector:

Report:

- exact file
- exact function
- reason
- evidence

Do not rely solely on source code inspection.

Use the active running runtime.

Deliverables

- Runtime Trace Engine
- Runtime Trace Repository
- Executive Trace Report
- Validation Results

Do not modify production routing logic unless explicitly approved.

This capability becomes part of MILES Developer Mode.

Runtime Instrumentation Layer

Objective

This is not an engineering proposal.

6. BuilderService

Each stage shall emit a structured trace event containing:

- timestamp
- stage
- file
- function
- provider
- connector
- workflow
- intent
- action
- input
- output
- executionTimeMs

Store traces in memory and write them to:

DATA/runtime_traces/

Run these commands through the live runtime:

- Improve MILES OS
- Check ORION Health
- Review Website

For each command produce a complete execution trace showing every stage.

Do not produce a proposal.

Implement the instrumentation.

Do not replace existing architecture.

Integrate into the current production pipeline.

Return the runtime trace files and a summary report.

Code Writer Capability Audit

Use the active production runtime.

Do not modify any files.

Do not generate proposals.

Determine whether MILES currently contains any component capable of generating complete replacement source files.

Search the entire MILES OS repository.

Look for classes, services, or modules that perform any of the following:

• writeFile
• fs.writeFile
• fs.writeFileSync
• createWriteStream
• patch generation
• replacement generation
• code generation
• source generation
• template generation

Also search for services named similarly to:

CodeWriter
ReplacementWriter
ReplacementGenerator
PatchEngine
PatchGenerator
CodeGenerator
EngineeringWriter
RuntimeWriter
TemplateEngine

For every match report:

- file
- function
- purpose
- whether it is currently invoked by EngineeringImprovementService

Finally answer:

1. Does a production code-generation engine exist?

2. If yes, why is EngineeringImprovementService not calling it?

3. If no, explicitly state:

"The current MILES runtime has no code-generation engine. EngineeringImprovementService can only generate engineering proposals."

Do not recommend changes.

Return evidence only.

BUILD 050

Runtime Dispatch Instrumentation

Objective

Instrument the live runtime dispatcher.

This is NOT an engineering improvement.

This is NOT a proposal.

This is NOT a planning task.

Requirements

Modify the runtime dispatcher itself to emit a dispatch trace for every request.

For every command log:

REQUEST RECEIVED

↓

PLANNER OUTPUT

↓

PROVIDER

↓

CONNECTOR

↓

BUILDER ACTION

↓

SERVICE NAME

↓

SERVICE FILE

↓

METHOD INVOKED

↓

RESULT

Write each trace to:

DATA/runtime_dispatch/runtime_dispatch.log

Do not execute EngineeringImprovementService to generate this report.

The instrumentation must occur inside the dispatcher so that every future request automatically records its execution path.

Success Criteria

After installation, execute:

STATUS

The runtime log must show the complete dispatch path from command receipt through the final service invocation.

"command": "MILES — INSTANTLY LIVE ACTIVATION DIRECTIVE

Objective:
Take the existing Instantly COO system from verified dry-run operation to controlled live operation. Do not build new architecture, registries, managers, planners, dispatchers, workers, connectors, or duplicate services.

Authoritative root:
D:\P2GC_Intelligence\MILES_ENTERPRISE

Known completed components include:
- InstantlyCOOWorker
- InstantlyApiClient
- InstantlyLiveProviderController
- InstantlyLiveIntegrationService
- InstantlyControlledWriteService
- ControlledWriteService
- ControlledWritePolicyService
- InstantlyCampaignOperator
- CampaignMonitoringEngine
- MarketingExecutionEngine
- ExecutiveDecisionEngine
- EnterpriseScheduler
- LiveProductionExecutionSystem
- LiveAutonomousBusinessMode
- ContinuousCOOLoopService
- WorkerDispatcher
- AutonomousWorkOrchestrator

Confirmed:
- INSTANTLY_API_KEY works.
- Live API health check returned HTTP 200.
- Campaign listing works.
- Campaign detail retrieval works.
- Campaign inventory works.
- Instantly COO Worker works.
- Dry-run execution already works.
- MILES_ENTERPRISE is the authoritative runtime.
- Do not use D:\P2GC_Intelligence\MILES_OS.

Mission:
1. Identify the exact production startup entry point currently used to run MILES.
2. Trace the existing “Run Instantly” command from command intake through:
   - intent planning
   - mission/work creation
   - worker routing
   - InstantlyCOOWorker
   - controlled-write policy
   - live provider controller
   - Instantly API
3. Identify every gate that forces dry-run or disables writes.
4. Do not globally remove safety controls.
5. Enable controlled live execution only for an allowlist of reversible Instantly operations:
   - HEALTH_CHECK
   - LIST_CAMPAIGNS
   - GET_CAMPAIGN
   - GENERATE_CAMPAIGN_REPORT
   - PAUSE_CAMPAIGN
6. Keep these operations approval-protected until separately validated:
   - RESUME_CAMPAIGN
   - START_CAMPAIGN
   - CREATE_CAMPAIGN
   - UPLOAD_LEADS
   - ASSIGN_SENDING_ACCOUNTS
   - DELETE_CAMPAIGN
   - DELETE_LEADS
   - CHANGE_EMAIL_COPY
   - INCREASE_DAILY_LIMIT
7. Run one controlled live canary using a non-destructive read operation first.
8. Run one reversible live write canary only after verification:
   - pause a specifically approved campaign
   - verify its live state
   - restore it only if restoration is separately approved
9. Record:
   - entry point
   - execution path
   - gate discovered
   - files changed
   - API request
   - API response
   - verification result
   - rollback status
10. If any required capability already exists, use it. Do not create another implementation.
11. If blocked, return the exact file, line, condition, and environment variable causing the block.
12. Do not modify unrelated systems.

Success condition:
The command “Run Instantly” reaches InstantlyCOOWorker, passes the controlled-write policy for an authorized operation, executes through InstantlyLiveProviderController, receives a verified live API result, records the outcome, and returns a concise COO summary.

Begin with discovery and execution tracing. Do not build anything unless the trace proves a required function is genuinely absent.",
